title: Policy
description: The one provider-neutral policy, .ai/repo/policy.yaml: budgets, verification, retention, enforcement and projections.

session.description: What the provider's episode events do beyond drawing the boundary: how much the start event hands the worker, and whether the compaction and end events record anything.

briefing_on_start.description: Hand the worker a briefing on the start event's standard output, which the provider adds to the context it is about to build. False restores the older silence, in which a continuation record is written and nothing loads it.

briefing_budget_lines.description: Hard cap on what the start event writes to the provider's context. Text that arrives in every episode is paid for in every episode.

checkpoint_on_compact.description: Record a derived checkpoint when the provider announces a compaction. A compaction discards the conversation while the work continues.

handover_on_end.description: Write a derived continuation record when an episode ends with its task still active.

ensure_server_on_start.description: On the start event, make sure the repository's shared server serves this checkout (`majordomus serve ensure`): a server is started when none answers, never built, and the briefing names where it stands. False leaves the server to the first MCP client.

record_sections.description: The sections a closed episode's record carries in its body, in order. The front matter is what a machine can prove; these are what the episode was for and how it turned out, composed from the worker's own checkpoints and decisions where it left any and from git and the ledger where it did not. A section named here with no writer in lib/derive.sh ends `session close` with exit 10 naming the section, so an unwritable section is a configuration error rather than a silently empty heading.

commit_record_on_end.description: Commit the record the end event publishes. Every surface that reads session records reads the tracked tree, so a record left in the working tree is written, validated, counted healthy and invisible. The commit carries that one path and runs no commit hook. False restores the older behaviour, in which the lifecycle wrote a record and nothing committed it.

push_record_on_end.description: Publish the record commit, as a fast-forward only and through the pre-push hook like any other push. That hook asks whether the task may be published, so the push often will not go out and the record travels with the worker's next push instead.

benchmark.description: How majordomus bench samples, and the thresholds bench --check and the command budgets apply.

use_cases.description: How use-case coverage is gated: per class of target, whether a gap fails, is reported, or is not looked at.
